The one dependency a Node application needs to start on EGRADX. It is the counterpart of the Java `egradx-sdk`. It brings sign-in and identity (`@babulvaibhav/egradx-auth`), the audit trail (`@babulvaibhav/egradx-audit`) and notifications (`@babulvaibhav/egradx-notification`). It connects them as Java's bridges do: auth's people are the audit trail's actors and notifications' recipients, and auth's reset links, invitations and codes go out as notifications. Everything an application uses from those packages, and from `@babulvaibhav/egradx-core`, `@babulvaibhav/egradx-observability` and `@babulvaibhav/egradx-migrations`, is exported from here too.

```ts
import { createEgradx, migrateEgradx } from '@babulvaibhav/egradx-sdk';
import { egradxErrors, egradxMiddleware, egradxRoutes } from '@babulvaibhav/egradx-sdk/express';

await migrateEgradx(databaseUrl, { application: (url) => migrateMyTables(url) });
const egradx = createEgradx({
  prisma,                                                        // the application's PrismaClient
  auth: { issuer: 'https://my-app.example', keys: { keystorePath: './keys', passphrase: process.env.EGRADX_KEY_PASSPHRASE! } },
  notifications: { templates: { directories: ['./notification-templates'] } },
});
await egradx.start();

const app = express();
app.use(egradxMiddleware(egradx));   // request ids, the request context, the caller from a bearer token
app.use(express.json());
app.use(myRoutes(egradx));           // egradx.auditor.record(...), egradx.notifications.messenger.send(...)
app.use(egradxRoutes(egradx));       // /egradx/auth/**, /egradx/audit/**, /egradx/notifications/**
app.use(...egradxErrors());          // 404, and every error as the contract's envelope
```

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `createEgradx(options)` | Creates auth, the auditor and notifications on the application's `PrismaClient`, connected, as Java's auto-configuration does. `options.auth`, `.audit` and `.notifications` are each library's own options (Java's `egradx.auth.*`, `egradx.audit.*`, `egradx.notification.*`); only `auth.issuer` and `auth.keys` are required. `start()` seeds the platform organization and its administrator and starts the periodic work; `close()` stops it. |
| `redis` option | Several instances acting as one: pass `createRedisCoordination({ url })` from `@babulvaibhav/egradx-redis` (a package of its own, not a dependency of this one). Sign-in attempts are counted in Redis (unless `auth.limiter` is given), role changes reach every instance's cache, and in-app notifications are pushed on every instance (unless `notifications.broadcaster` is given). `start()` and `close()` start and close it with the rest; it never waits for Redis. |
| `migrateEgradx(databaseUrl, { application?, afterAudit? })` | Every library's tables, in Java's order, into the history tables Java uses. egradx-auth's come first, then the application's own (`application`), then egradx-audit's, `afterAudit` (Java's `EgradxAuditSchemaCallback`) and egradx-notification's, then egradx-events' if `@babulvaibhav/egradx-events` is installed. |
| `@babulvaibhav/egradx-sdk/express`: `egradxMiddleware`, `egradxRoutes`, `egradxErrors` | The Express parts, in the order to register them. `egradxRoutes` takes anything with `auth`, `auditor` and `notifications`. Also exported: everything from `@babulvaibhav/egradx-express` and the libraries' Express modules (`requireAuthority`, `currentCaller`, …). |
| Observability | Each library is timed and traced through `@babulvaibhav/egradx-observability` (`observations`, `metrics`). As in Java, registering an OpenTelemetry SDK and its exporters is the application's choice; OIM's `telemetry.ts` is an example. |

## Tests

An application whose only EGRADX dependency is this package. The tests check:
- the migrations run in Java's order;
- sign-in works, and is audited with its actor;
- the inbox serves the signed-in person and refuses anyone else;
- the application's own route audits its change and sends a message in its transaction;
- a reset link goes out as an email;
- a `redis` coordination is given the limiter's settings and the libraries, publishes the live pushes, and is started and closed with them;
- the application's errors and unknown routes come back in the contract's envelope.

OIM's Node backend is built on it.

### ControlManager

Starts every registered Control when the application is ready, and stops them when it shuts down, each in the order
registered. As Java's ControlManager, which does so on Spring's context refreshed and closed events: here the
application calls `start()` once it is ready and `stop()` on shutdown. A control that fails to start fails the
startup, and those after it are not started; one that fails to stop is logged, and the rest still stop.

### EgradxAuditEvent

Something worth an audit record: who did what, to what, with what result. Actions are named
`category.entity.verb`, lower case with underscores (`auth.password.changed`). Every value is checked
when the event is built, so a malformed event fails where it is written, not inside a transaction.
`before`, `after` and `details` are stored as JSON; secrets are redacted by key, but should not be passed.

in-process, no separate service. As Java's EgradxAuthService.

```ts

```

Continues the session a refresh token belongs to: a new access token, and a new refresh token in place of the one
presented, which is retired (rotation). The session keeps its organization and its expiry. A retired token still
renews the session for the reuse grace after it was replaced, so two callers refreshing with it at once both carry
on; presented after that, it is taken as stolen: the whole session ends (auth.session.reused) with SESSION_REVOKED.

### EgradxBulkExpander

Turns bulk sends into deliveries, one page of recipients per call, each page one transaction: lock the
oldest send still expanding (skipping any another instance holds), take the next page after
expanded_through, resolve, render once per language, write the deliveries, move on. A page that fails
rolls back and is done again; nobody is expanded twice or skipped. Users without an address, or who
opted out, are counted, not failed. A template that no longer renders fails the send; anything else is
retried on the next poll. As Java's EgradxBulkExpander.

#### Constructors

### EgradxChannelConfigResolver

Finds the configuration a channel uses for an organization: its own, else the all-organizations one.
An organization's own that is disabled is returned as it is, not skipped: disabled means "this
organization does not send on this channel". The row is read on every call, so an edit applies on the
next send everywhere; decrypting (deliberately slow) happens once per distinct content.

### EgradxEmailChannel

Email over SMTP, through nodemailer. Which server sends is decided per message: the organization's
stored configuration (disabled: it sends no email), else the all-organizations one, else the
application's own. Stored configurations get their own transporter, built once per distinct content,
with timeouts always set. A rejected recipient or a message that can't be built is permanent; a server
down, slow or refusing the credentials is retried. As Java's EgradxEmailChannel.

### EgradxEmailCodeService

Six-digit codes emailed for signing in without a password, and for signing up (docs/auth/sign-in-methods.md). As
Java's EgradxEmailCodeService.

Asking for a sign-in code answers the same whether or not the address has an account; a code is sent only to an
active one. Checking a code answers EMAIL_CODE_INVALID alike for a wrong code, an unknown address and no code at all.
Wrong codes count, and the count is kept though the check is refused.

Sign-up makes, when its code is entered, the account, a new organization it administers, and a session there.

### EgradxFileTemplates

Templates shipped as files, indexed once when created; the counterpart of Java's classpath templates,
with the same layout under each directory:

  order.shipped/email.subject.txt       subject, default locale
  order.shipped/email.body.html         body; .html means values are HTML-escaped
  order.shipped/email.fr.body.html      French
  order.shipped/sms.body.txt            .txt means values are inserted as they are

The application's directories are searched in order, then the library's; the first holding a template
for a key, channel and locale supplies it. Every file is checked now: its name, its type being
declared, compiling, and using only declared variables. A typo fails startup, not a send.

### EgradxHandlebarsRenderer

Handlebars, strict and treating templates as untrusted, as Java's EgradxHandlebarsRenderer, with this SDK's own
renderer (./handlebars.ts), held to contracts/notification-templates/rendering-test-vectors.json:
- a top-level variable the template uses but the model lacks fails the render, naming it;
- the model is converted to plain data first (objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans; dates as Java's
  Instant.toString()), so a template reads what it is given and nothing else; partials are refused;
- escaping follows the format: HTML-escaped into an HTML body, verbatim into text. Subjects are text, with
  line breaks collapsed to spaces, since a mail subject is one header line.
Compiled templates are cached by the source's cacheKey, bounded in number.

- [`EgradxTemplateRenderer`](#egradxtemplaterenderer)

one stored for all organizations, then the template files. Within a layer the locale falls back

### EgradxLogShipper

Ships the application's log lines to an EgradxLogSink, with the trace, request, person and organization each was
logged for, as Java's EgradxLogShippingAppender. Best effort: logging only adds the line to a bounded queue; a timer
sends batches, one at a time; when the queue is full, lines are dropped and counted, so shipping can never slow the
application or fill its memory.

  const shipper = new EgradxLogShipper(events.logSink(), { service: 'orders' });
  const log = pino({ ...egradxPinoOptions() }, pino.multistream([{ stream: process.stdout }, { stream: egradxShippingDestination(shipper) }]));

Any other logger can call `offer` itself.

### EgradxMessenger

The way to send a message: to users or addresses, on the channel the caller names, from a template or
ready-made content. Returns once queued; nothing is sent here. Resolves each user to an address and a
locale, renders once per locale, and queues one message per locale, all in one transaction (the
surrounding one, if any): every locale's message is queued or none is. It never publishes an in-app
notification; a caller wanting both makes both calls. As Java's EgradxMessenger.

### EgradxNotificationBacklogGauge

egradx.notification.delivery.backlog: PENDING deliveries that are due now (`egradx.state` = `due`) and those waiting for
a retry (`waiting`). A `due` count that keeps growing means sends are falling behind, or no dispatcher is running. Counted
in one pass over the PENDING rows, and kept for `refreshMs`, so that several instances each scraped often do not each
count the table. As Java's EgradxNotificationBacklogGauge, with one difference: a gauge is read synchronously here, so a
stale count starts a recount and the last count is reported meanwhile (NaN before the first).

```ts
): EgradxNotificationBacklogGauge;
```

### EgradxNotificationDispatcher

Delivers what the outbox holds. Each round claims a batch of due deliveries in one statement, sends
them concurrently outside any transaction, then records each result on its own; nothing holds a
connection or a lock while a provider is answering.

Safe to run on every instance, and alongside Java's dispatcher on the same database: claiming uses
FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and counts the attempt up front, hiding the row for the lease; every result is
written only if the row still has that attempt and is PENDING, so a slow sender's result whose lease
lapsed is discarded rather than overwriting a newer attempt. Delivery is at-least-once. As Java's
EgradxNotificationDispatcher.

#### Constructors

##### Constructor

```ts
new EgradxNotificationDispatcher(
   prisma, 
   channels, 
   attachments, 
   settings, 
   backoff, 
   retention, 
   bulk, 
   now, 
   log, 
   observations?, 
   metrics?
): EgradxNotificationDispatcher;
```

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| ------ | ------ | ------ |
| `prisma` | [`PrismaLike`](#prismalike) | - |
| `channels` | [`EgradxChannelRegistry`](#egradxchannelregistry) | - |
| `attachments` | [`EgradxAttachmentStore`](#egradxattachmentstore) | - |
| `settings` | [`DispatcherSettings`](#dispatchersettings) | - |
| `backoff` | [`EgradxBackoffPolicy`](#egradxbackoffpolicy) | - |
| `retention` | [`RetentionSettings`](#retentionsettings) | - |
| `bulk` | [`EgradxBulkExpander`](#egradxbulkexpander) \| `undefined` | - |
| `now` | () => `Date` | - |
| `log` | [`NotificationLog`](#notificationlog) | - |
| `observations?` | [`EgradxObservations`](#egradxobservations) | egradx.notification.delivery, one per attempt, continuing the submitting request's trace. |
| `metrics?` | [`EgradxMetrics`](#egradxmetrics) | egradx.notification.delivery.dead and .discarded. |

###### Returns

[`EgradxNotificationDispatcher`](#egradxnotificationdispatcher)

### EgradxNotificationPublisher

Publishes in-app notifications: one row per call, whatever the audience; who sees an organization- or
platform-wide one is worked out when an inbox is read. This never sends anything anywhere else.

### EgradxNotificationType

One kind of message an application sends (`order.shipped`) and the variables its templates may use.
The declaration makes rendering strict: a required variable missing from the model is refused, an
optional one may be left out, a model entry that is neither is refused (it is almost always a
misspelling), and a template using an undeclared variable is refused when loaded or saved.
As Java's EgradxNotificationType.

### EgradxObservations

The one way egradx code times an operation: a timer `egradx.<module>.<operation>` (seconds) when the application has an
OpenTelemetry meter provider, a span "<module> <operation>" when it has a tracer provider, and nothing when it has
neither. Every observation carries `egradx.outcome`: `success` unless the code sets another, `error` if it throws
without having set one, so all samples of one timer have the same tag keys. Work handed to another thread or process
is a send and later a receive: send captures the trace into an EgradxTraceContext to store with the work; receive
and consumer continue it where the work is picked up. As Java's EgradxObservations.

#### Constructors

##### Constructor

```ts
new EgradxObservations(options?): EgradxObservations;
```

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `options?` | \{ `meterProvider?`: `MeterProvider`; `tracerProvider?`: `TracerProvider`; \} |
| `options.meterProvider?` | `MeterProvider` |
| `options.tracerProvider?` | `TracerProvider` |

###### Returns

[`EgradxObservations`](#egradxobservations)

#### Properties

| Property | Modifier | Type | Default value | Description |
| ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ |
| <a id="property-channel-4"></a> `CHANNEL` | `readonly` | `"egradx.channel"` | `"egradx.channel"` | - |
| <a id="property-error"></a> `ERROR` | `readonly` | `"error"` | `"error"` | - |
| <a id="property-outcome-1"></a> `OUTCOME` | `readonly` | `"egradx.outcome"` | `"egradx.outcome"` | - |
| <a id="property-request_id"></a> `REQUEST_ID` | `readonly` | `"egradx.request.id"` | `"egradx.request.id"` | High-cardinality key for the request id, so a span can be found by the id in an error message. |
| <a id="property-success"></a> `SUCCESS` | `readonly` | `"success"` | `"success"` | - |

### EgradxOidcClient

Talks to OpenID Connect providers: reads their discovery documents, builds the authorization URL, exchanges the code
for tokens and verifies the ID token against the provider's published keys. Discovery documents are cached for an
hour, and so are key sets (by jose). As Java's EgradxOidcClient.

### EgradxOidcService

Signing in with OpenID Connect providers — Google, Zoho, or any other configured — and linking them to accounts
(docs/auth/sign-in-methods.md). As Java's EgradxOidcService.

A round trip is: start (the browser is sent to the provider), callback (the provider sends it back; what it proved is
stored under a one-time result code and the browser is sent to the frontend), then exchange (the frontend trades the
result code for a session). Every step keeps its state in the database, so each may reach a different instance.

#### Constructors

##### Constructor

```ts
new EgradxOidcService(
   prisma, 
   providers, 
   authService, 
   emailCodes, 
   invitations, 
   senders, 
   signupSettings, 
   settings, 
   links, 
   warn, 
   observations?
): EgradxOidcService;
```

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `prisma` | [`PrismaLike`](#prismalike) |
| `providers` | [`EgradxSignInProviders`](#egradxsigninproviders) |
| `authService` | [`EgradxAuthService`](#egradxauthservice) |
| `emailCodes` | [`EgradxEmailCodeService`](#egradxemailcodeservice) |
| `invitations` | [`EgradxInvitationService`](#egradxinvitationservice) |
| `senders` | `SenderHolder` |
| `signupSettings` | [`SignupSettings`](#signupsettings) |
| `settings` | [`OidcSettings`](#oidcsettings) |
| `links` | [`LinkSettings`](#linksettings) |
| `warn` | (`message`) => `void` |
| `observations?` | [`EgradxObservations`](#egradxobservations) |

###### Returns

[`EgradxOidcService`](#egradxoidcservice)

#### Methods

##### callback()

```ts
callback(providerId, parameters): Promise<string>;
```

The provider's callback: checks it and returns where on the frontend to send the browser — with `code` (to
exchange), `linked` (a provider linked from the profile), or `error`. Never throws for what the provider or the
browser sent.

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `providerId` | `string` |
| `parameters` | `Record`\<`string`, `string`\> |

###### Returns

`Promise`\<`string`\>

##### exchange()

```ts
exchange(
   code, 
   organizationId, 
   invitationToken
): Promise<EgradxAuthResult>;
```

Trades the result code for a session — or says why not. A code that ends in SIGNUP_REQUIRED or
ORG_SELECTION_REQUIRED stays usable for the next step. OIDC_CODE_INVALID, OIDC_EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED,
ORG_SELECTION_REQUIRED (400); AUTH_NO_ACCOUNT, ORG_ACCESS_DENIED, ORG_SUSPENDED (403); IDENTITY_LINK_REQUIRED,
SIGNUP_REQUIRED (409).

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `code` | `string` |
| `organizationId` | `string` \| `null` |
| `invitationToken` | `string` \| `null` |

###### Returns

`Promise`\<[`EgradxAuthResult`](#egradxauthresult)\>

##### signInMethods()

```ts
signInMethods(userId): Promise<EgradxSignInMethodsDto>;
```

How the person can sign in: whether they have a password, and the providers linked.

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `userId` | `string` |

###### Returns

`Promise`\<[`EgradxSignInMethodsDto`](#egradxsigninmethodsdto)\>

##### signInOptions()

```ts
signInOptions(): EgradxSignInOptionsDto;
```

What a sign-in page can offer here.

###### Returns

[`EgradxSignInOptionsDto`](#egradxsigninoptionsdto)

##### signup()

```ts
signup(code, organizationName): Promise<EgradxAuthResult>;
```

Signs up with the provider's verified email, after SIGNUP_REQUIRED: an account with no password, a new organization
it administers, the provider linked, and a session there. SIGNUP_DISABLED (403); OIDC_CODE_INVALID,
OIDC_EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED, SIGNUP_EMAIL_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED (400); EMAIL_IN_USE, ORGANIZATION_NAME_IN_USE, IDENTITY_IN_USE (409).

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `code` | `string` |
| `organizationName` | `string` |

###### Returns

`Promise`\<[`EgradxAuthResult`](#egradxauthresult)\>

##### start()

```ts
start(
   providerId, 
   returnTo, 
   linkUserId
): Promise<string>;
```

Starts a round trip to the provider and returns where to send the browser. `returnTo` is a path on the frontend to
come back to (anything else is dropped); `linkUserId` links the provider to that signed-in account, rather than sign
in. OIDC_PROVIDER_UNKNOWN (404); OIDC_FAILED when the provider cannot be reached (its discovery document cannot be read).

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `providerId` | `string` |
| `returnTo` | `string` \| `null` \| `undefined` |
| `linkUserId` | `string` \| `null` |

###### Returns

`Promise`\<`string`\>

##### unlink()

```ts
unlink(
   userId, 
   organizationId, 
   identityId
): Promise<void>;
```

Removes a linked provider: NOT_FOUND when it is not one of the person's; SIGN_IN_METHOD_REQUIRED when it would leave them no way to sign in.

| ------ | ------ |
| `userId` | `string` |
| `organizationId` | `string` \| `null` |
| `identityId` | `string` |

### EgradxOidcSignInProvider

Any OpenID Connect provider: the authorization code flow with PKCE, `state` and `nonce`, and the ID token checked
against the provider's published keys (EgradxOidcClient). Configured with `type: 'oidc'` (the default), an `issuer`
and a client. As Java's EgradxOidcSignInProvider.

### EgradxOutboxTransport

The default transport: writes the message and one PENDING delivery per address, for the dispatcher to
deliver; needs no broker. As Java's EgradxOutboxTransport:
- it joins the surrounding egradxTransaction (or `tx`), so an order confirmation goes out if and only if
  the order commits; without one it runs in its own;
- everything knowable before sending is checked here, on the caller's side: the channel exists and is
  configured for the organization, every address is well-formed, the limits hold;
- the request id is stored with the message, so its deliveries can be found by the request that sent them.

#### Constructors

##### Constructor

```ts
new EgradxOutboxTransport(
   prisma, 
   channels, 
   attachments, 
   limits, 
   now, 
   enqueued, 
   observations?, 
   metrics?
): EgradxOutboxTransport;
```

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| ------ | ------ | ------ |
| `prisma` | [`PrismaLike`](#prismalike) | - |
| `channels` | [`EgradxChannelRegistry`](#egradxchannelregistry) | - |
| `attachments` | [`EgradxAttachmentStore`](#egradxattachmentstore) | - |
| `limits` | [`OutboxLimits`](#outboxlimits) | - |
| `now` | () => `Date` | - |
| `enqueued` | () => `void` | Wakes the dispatcher once the deliveries are committed. |
| `observations?` | [`EgradxObservations`](#egradxobservations) | egradx.notification.submit; each message stores the trace and request id of the request that submitted it. |
| `metrics?` | [`EgradxMetrics`](#egradxmetrics) | - |

###### Returns

[`EgradxOutboxTransport`](#egradxoutboxtransport)

#### Methods

##### submit()

```ts

```

###### Parameters

| `options?` | \{ `tx?`: [`SqlClient`](#sqlclient); \} |
| `options.tx?` | [`SqlClient`](#sqlclient) |

`Promise`\<`string`\>

### EgradxSessionService

A person's sessions: listing them, ending one, ending every one on every device at once. Ending a session revokes its
refresh tokens and refuses its access tokens on their next request (sid); ending all of them also sets
sessions_valid_after, so that access tokens already issued are refused. As Java's EgradxSessionService.

#### Constructors

##### Constructor

```ts
new EgradxSessionService(
   prisma, 
   authService, 
   observations?
): EgradxSessionService;
```

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `prisma` | [`PrismaLike`](#prismalike) |
| `authService` | [`EgradxAuthService`](#egradxauthservice) |
| `observations?` | [`EgradxObservations`](#egradxobservations) |

###### Returns

[`EgradxSessionService`](#egradxsessionservice)

#### Methods

##### cutOff()

```ts
cutOff(
   tx, 
   userId, 
   time
): Promise<void>;
```

Sessions_valid_after now, every session ended (ALL_ENDED) and every refresh token revoked: every access token issued before is refused.

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `tx` | [`SqlClient`](#sqlclient) |
| `userId` | `string` |
| `time` | `Date` |

###### Returns

`Promise`\<`void`\>

##### endMine()

```ts
endMine(
   userId, 
   organizationId, 
   sessionId
): Promise<void>;
```

Ends one of the person's sessions (ENDED): another device's, or this one. Its refresh tokens stop working at once,
its access tokens on their next request. NOT_FOUND when it is not one of theirs still going: the same answer for
both, so an id says nothing about anyone else's sessions.

###### Parameters

### EgradxSignInProviders

The sign-in providers in use: those configured under `oidc.providers`, each made by the SignInProviderFactory of its
`type`, and those the application passes in `oidc.extraProviders`. Knows nothing of any particular provider. As Java's
EgradxSignInProviders.

Every provider needs `oidc.callbackBaseUrl` (for its redirect URI) and `links.baseUrl` (where the browser lands
afterwards); a configured one also needs its client id and secret. A provider missing any of them is left out, with a
warning.

#### Constructors

##### Constructor

```ts
new EgradxSignInProviders(
   settings, 
   linksBaseUrl,

   factories?, 
   registered?
): EgradxSignInProviders;
```

factory of a built-in type replaces it.

### EgradxTraceContext

Where a piece of work came from, in a form that can be written into a database row or a message and picked up again
later: what a tracer's propagator writes (the W3C traceparent, and tracestate or baggage if any), plus the requestId of
the HTTP request that started it. Without a tracer only the request id is there, which is still enough to find every
log line and row a request produced. Immutable; never throws on bad input. As Java's EgradxTraceContext, whose text
every SDK writes and reads alike (contracts/test-vectors/observability.json).

### EgradxWebhookChannel

An HTTP POST of JSON to the address, for systems rather than people. Signed with HMAC-SHA256 over
"<timestamp>.<body>" when the configuration has a secret; Idempotency-Key is the delivery id. 2xx is
delivered; 408, 425, 429, 5xx and not connecting are retried; any other 4xx is permanent. HTTPS only
unless allowHttp. As Java's EgradxWebhookChannel, with the same payload and headers.

only approved templates, so a notification is mapped, in the `templates` setting, to its template and

### AuditActorResolver

Says who is signed in: used to say who acted when an event doesn't, and to decide what a caller of the
endpoints may read. Without one, records made in a request name no one and the endpoints answer 401,
as in Java without egradx-audit-auth.

```ts
  | undefined;
```

  \| `undefined`

##### record()

```ts
record(event, options?): Promise<void>;
```

Records an event. A success (WITH_TRANSACTION) is written in `tx`, or in the surrounding
`auditor.transaction(...)`, so it commits with the change or not at all; a failure to write it
throws, failing the change. A failure or refusal (INDEPENDENT), or anything recorded outside a
transaction, is written at once on its own and survives a rollback; a failure to write it is
logged, never thrown.

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `event` | [`EgradxAuditEvent`](#egradxauditevent) |
| `options?` | [`RecordOptions`](#recordoptions) |

###### Returns

`Promise`\<`void`\>

##### recordChange()

```ts
recordChange(
   action, 
   entityType, 
   entityId, 
   before, 
   after, 
   options?
): Promise<void>;
```

| `before` | `unknown` |

### EgradxAttemptLimiter

Limits wrong passwords: per account from one address, and per address across all accounts. Only
failures count; a success clears the count for that account from that address. There is deliberately
no limit on an account alone, which would let anyone lock its owner out. As Java's EgradxAttemptLimiter.

Each method may return a Promise, for a limiter that counts somewhere shared across instances
(`@babulvaibhav/egradx-redis`); the callers await it.

#### Methods

```ts
failed(key, clientAddress): void | Promise<void>;
```

###### Parameters

| ------ | ------ |
| `key` | `string` |
| `clientAddress` | `string` \| `null` |

`void` \| `Promise`\<`void`\>

```ts
retryAfter(key, clientAddress): number | Promise<number | undefined> | undefined;
```

### EgradxMetrics

Counters, gauges and timers for what has no natural span: messages given up on, the size of a backlog, open
connections. Timed operations should use EgradxObservations instead, which gives a timer and a span from one call.
Names start with `egradx.`; tags are alternating key, value pairs, checked by EgradxTagRules even when metrics are off,
so a bad tag fails a test. As Java's EgradxMetrics.

#### Methods

##### count()

```ts
count(
   name, 
   amount, 
   ...tags
): void;
```

Adds `amount` to a counter; zero or less records nothing.

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `name` | `string` |
| `amount` | `number` |
| ...`tags` | `string`[] |

###### Returns

`void`

##### enabled()

```ts
enabled(): boolean;
```

Whether anything is recorded. Lets a caller skip work that only feeds a metric.

###### Returns

`boolean`

##### gauge()

```ts
gauge(
   name, 
   read, 
   ...tags
): void;
```

Reads `read()` whenever metrics are collected.

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `name` | `string` |
| `read` | () => `number` |
| ...`tags` | `string`[] |

###### Returns

`void`

##### increment()

```ts
increment(name, ...tags): void;
```

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `name` | `string` |
| ...`tags` | `string`[] |

###### Returns

`void`

##### record()

```ts
record(
   name, 
   durationMs, 
   ...tags
): void;
```

Records a duration in milliseconds, as seconds (Micrometer's base unit for timers).

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `name` | `string` |
| `durationMs` | `number` |
| ...`tags` | `string`[] |

###### Returns

`void`

### EgradxSignInProvider

One way of signing in elsewhere — Google, Zoho, any OpenID Connect provider, or a provider of an application's own
(GitHub, a company's identity server). egradx-auth drives the round trip — state, PKCE, the callback, linking the
account, the session — and asks the provider only for the two steps that differ between them: where to send the
browser, and who came back. As Java's EgradxSignInProvider.

Adding a provider is writing a class: implement this interface (or extend EgradxOidcSignInProvider for one that
speaks OpenID Connect) and either pass it in `oidc.extraProviders`, or pass a SignInProviderFactory in
`oidc.providerFactories` so that it is configured under `oidc.providers.<id>.type`. No existing class changes.

#### Properties

| Property | Modifier | Type | Description |
| ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ |
| <a id="property-id-14"></a> `id` | `readonly` | `string` | The id in the URLs (`/egradx/auth/oidc/{id}/start`) and in stored identities: `google`, `github`. |
| <a id="property-name-13"></a> `name` | `readonly` | `string` | Shown on the button: `Google`. |
| <a id="property-trustemail-1"></a> `trustEmail` | `readonly` | `boolean` | Whether this provider's verified emails prove ownership of the address, so that a sign-in whose email matches an existing account is linked to it automatically. Only for providers that check addresses themselves. |

#### Methods

##### authorizationUrl()

```ts
authorizationUrl(request): string | Promise<string>;
```

Where to send the browser to sign in. Throws EgradxSignInProviderException if the provider cannot be reached.

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `request` | [`EgradxSignInAuthorization`](#egradxsigninauthorization) |

###### Returns

`string` \| `Promise`\<`string`\>

##### complete()

```ts
complete(callback): 
  | EgradxProviderIdentity
| Promise<EgradxProviderIdentity>;
```

Who the provider says signed in, from its callback: exchange the code, check what comes back. Throws (or rejects
with) EgradxSignInProviderException if the provider cannot be reached, or its answer does not check out.

###### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `callback` | [`EgradxSignInCallback`](#egradxsignincallback) |

###### Returns

  \| [`EgradxProviderIdentity`](#egradxprovideridentity)
  \| `Promise`\<[`EgradxProviderIdentity`](#egradxprovideridentity)\>

### EgradxAuditActorType

```ts
type EgradxAuditActorType = "USER" | "ANONYMOUS" | "SYSTEM" | "UNKNOWN";
```

USER: signed in. ANONYMOUS: not signed in. SYSTEM: the application itself. UNKNOWN: in a request, but nothing said by whom.

***

### EgradxAuditDurability

```ts
type EgradxAuditDurability = "WITH_TRANSACTION" | "INDEPENDENT";
```

Whether a record shares the fate of the transaction it was made in. Unset: a SUCCESS is
WITH_TRANSACTION (commits with the change, or not at all) and anything else INDEPENDENT (stored at
once, surviving the caller's rollback).

***

### EgradxAuditOutcome

```ts
type EgradxAuditOutcome = "SUCCESS" | "FAILURE" | "DENIED";
```

How the audited attempt ended.

***

### EgradxBulkSendStatus

```ts
type EgradxBulkSendStatus = "EXPANDING" | "COMPLETE" | "FAILED";
```

***

### EgradxDeliveryResult

```ts
type EgradxDeliveryResult = 
  | {
  kind: "sent";
  providerMessageId: string | null;
}
  | {
  kind: "retryable";
  reason: string;
}
  | {
  kind: "permanent";
  reason: string;
};
```

What happened when a channel tried to deliver one message to one address. "Retryable" and "permanent"
call for opposite responses, and only a channel can tell them apart; one that can't should answer
retryable. A channel that throws is treated as retryable.

### accountTokens

```ts
const accountTokens: object;
```

The tokens in password-reset and invitation links, as Java's EgradxAccountTokens:

verifier are stored, so a database dump yields no working link.

### EgradxTagRules

```ts
const EgradxTagRules: object;
```

What may be a metric name or a metric tag, checked on every call so that a mistake fails a test instead of taking down a
metrics backend. As Java's EgradxTagRules, with its messages.

Every distinct combination of tag values is a separate time series. A tag whose values are unbounded (an organization
id, a user id, a request id) grows that set without limit, and ids and addresses are personal data besides. They
belong on spans, never on meters. So names start with `egradx.`, tag keys that name an id, an address, a URL or a path
are refused, and values that look like a UUID or are longer than 64 characters are refused.

#### Type Declaration

| Name | Type | Description |
| ------ | ------ | ------ |
| <a id="property-max_value_length"></a> `MAX_VALUE_LENGTH` | `number` | - |
| <a id="property-prefix"></a> `PREFIX` | `string` | - |
| `checkName()` | (`name`) => `string` | A meter or observation name: `egradx.` then dot-separated lower-case words. |
| `checkSegment()` | (`segment`) => `string` | One module or operation segment of a name, such as `notification` or `bulk.expansion`. |
| `checkTag()` | (`key`, `value`) => `void` | - |
| `checkTags()` | (`keyValues`) => `Record`\<`string`, `string`\> | Checks alternating key, value pairs and returns them as attributes. |

### checkTemplate()

```ts
function checkTemplate(
   type, 
   source, 
   renderer
): void;
```

Refuses a template that does not compile, or that uses a variable its type does not declare, by
rendering it once with a stand-in for every declared variable. Best effort: a variable used only in a
branch the stand-ins don't take isn't seen here, but rendering is strict, so it still fails at send.
The stand-in is an empty map, as in Java: nothing to iterate, empty nested fields.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `type` | [`EgradxNotificationType`](#egradxnotificationtype) |
| `source` | [`EgradxTemplateSource`](#egradxtemplatesource) |
| `renderer` | [`EgradxTemplateRenderer`](#egradxtemplaterenderer) |

#### Returns

`void`

### createEgradx()

```ts
function createEgradx(options): Egradx;
```

Everything, on the application's PrismaClient, as Java's egradx-sdk brings it: egradx-auth, egradx-audit and
egradx-notification, with egradx-audit-auth and egradx-notification-auth connecting them. The libraries are created in
the order the bridges need: auth, then the audit trail and notifications, each told about auth before auth starts.

  await migrateEgradx(databaseUrl);
  const egradx = createEgradx({ prisma, auth: { issuer, keys: { keystorePath, passphrase } } });
  await egradx.start();

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `options` | [`EgradxOptions`](#egradxoptions) |

#### Returns

[`Egradx`](#egradx)

### egradxTransaction()

```ts
function egradxTransaction<R>(
   prisma, 
   fn, 
   options?
): Promise<R>;
```

Runs `fn` in a Prisma transaction that every EGRADX library joins without being passed it, as every
Spring library joins one transaction manager's: an audit record commits with the change, an in-app
notification is pushed only once it has. Nested calls join the outer transaction.

#### Type Parameters

| Type Parameter |
| ------ |
| `R` |

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `prisma` | [`PrismaLike`](#prismalike) |
| `fn` | (`tx`) => `Promise`\<`R`\> |
| `options?` | \{ `requiresNew?`: `boolean`; `timeout?`: `number`; \} |
| `options.requiresNew?` | `boolean` |
| `options.timeout?` | `number` |

#### Returns

`Promise`\<`R`\>

### migrate()

```ts
function migrate(options): Promise<MigrateResult>;
```

Applies the migrations in `location` that the history table doesn't list yet, in version order, each
in its own transaction. History rows, descriptions and checksums are written exactly as Flyway 10
writes them, and the checksums of migrations already applied are verified, so Java's migrators and
this one can take turns on the same database. Concurrent runs (several instances starting together)
are serialised with an advisory lock.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `options` | [`MigrateOptions`](#migrateoptions) |

#### Returns

`Promise`\<[`MigrateResult`](#migrateresult)\>

***

### migrateEgradx()

```ts
function migrateEgradx(databaseUrl, options?): Promise<void>;
```

Creates and upgrades every library's tables, in Java's order, into the history tables Java uses: egradx-auth's, then
the application's own (`application`), then egradx-audit's and egradx-notification's, and egradx-events' and
egradx-file-storage's when `@babulvaibhav/egradx-events` or `@babulvaibhav/egradx-file-storage` is installed (as Java
migrates their tables whenever they are on the classpath). So any SDK's application can start first on a database another SDK's created.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `databaseUrl` | `string` |
| `options` | [`MigrateEgradxOptions`](#migrateegradxoptions) |

#### Returns

`Promise`\<`void`\>

### publishAuditEvent()

```ts
function publishAuditEvent(event, options?): Promise<void>;
```

Publishes an audit event, as a Java library publishes one as a Spring event: @babulvaibhav/egradx-audit stores it
